questions.question: In the context of artificial neurons used in deep learning, what is the primary role of the activation function?
questions.choice_A: Introduce nonlinearity so networks can approximate complex, non-linear functions
questions.choice_B: Scale inputs to a unit norm to stabilize training
questions.choice_C: Ensure outputs are strictly positive to avoid vanishing gradients
questions.choice_D: Reduce the number of parameters by sharing weights across layers

questions.question: Which statement best describes a deep neural network layer composed of linear transformations followed by activations?
questions.choice_A: It is equivalent to a single linear transformation regardless of depth
questions.choice_B: Multiple linear layers without nonlinearities collapse to one linear map, but with nonlinearities they can approximate arbitrary functions
questions.choice_C: Adding more linear layers always reduces expressivity
questions.choice_D: Nonlinearities are only required in the final output layer

questions.question: Which statement about encoder, decoder, and decoder-only transformer variants is most accurate?
questions.choice_A: Encoders and decoders both use causal masks by default
questions.choice_B: Decoder-only models include cross-attention layers to attend to encoder outputs
questions.choice_C: Encoder blocks use bidirectional self-attention, while decoder-only blocks use causal self-attention without cross-attention
questions.choice_D: Decoders cannot attend to previously generated tokens

questions.question: Why is the dot product in scaled dot-product attention divided by $\sqrt{d_k}$?
questions.choice_A: To ensure the softmax outputs are uniform
questions.choice_B: To make $Q$ and $K$ orthogonal on average
questions.choice_C: To increase the magnitude of gradients in early layers
questions.choice_D: To prevent large dot products in high dimensions from saturating the softmax, stabilizing training

questions.question: What is the main benefit of multi-head attention over single-head attention?
questions.choice_A: It allows the model to attend to information from multiple representation subspaces in parallel
questions.choice_B: It reduces computational complexity from quadratic to linear in sequence length
questions.choice_C: It eliminates the need for positional information
questions.choice_D: It guarantees orthogonality between attention patterns

questions.question: What problem do positional encodings or embeddings solve in transformers?
questions.choice_A: They compress the vocabulary into a smaller set of tokens
questions.choice_B: They inject order information into token representations, which self-attention alone does not capture
questions.choice_C: They prevent overfitting by acting as a regularizer
questions.choice_D: They normalize token vectors to unit length

questions.question: Which description best captures subword tokenization such as BPE or WordPiece for LLMs?
questions.choice_A: It enforces fixed-length tokens to align with GPU memory layouts
questions.choice_B: It maps each character to a unique token to maximize coverage
questions.choice_C: It segments text into frequently occurring subword units, balancing vocabulary size with the ability to compose rare words
questions.choice_D: It uses a fixed dictionary of words with an out-of-vocabulary (OOV) token for unknown words

questions.question: In a standard transformer block, what best characterizes the position-wise feed-forward network (FFN/MLP)?
questions.choice_A: A single linear layer that mixes information across sequence positions
questions.choice_B: A convolution that introduces local spatial inductive biases
questions.choice_C: A recurrent unit that maintains hidden state across tokens
questions.choice_D: Two linear layers with a nonlinearity (often with expansion then projection), applied independently to each position

questions.question: What is the primary reason for applying layer normalization in transformer blocks?
questions.choice_A: Stabilize and standardize activations within a layer to improve optimization dynamics
questions.choice_B: Reduce model size by tying parameters across layers
questions.choice_C: Increase expressivity by adding nonlinearity
questions.choice_D: Decrease sequence length by downsampling

questions.question: Where are most parameters typically concentrated in a transformer-based LLM?
questions.choice_A: In positional encoding tables
questions.choice_B: In the projection matrices of attention (e.g., $W_Q, W_K, W_V, W_O$) and in the MLP/FFN layers
questions.choice_C: In the layer normalization scale and bias
questions.choice_D: In the residual skip connections

questions.question: Which sequence of operations best describes the dataflow in a pre-norm transformer block during a forward pass?
questions.choice_A: Self-attention → Residual add → LayerNorm → MLP → Residual add → LayerNorm
questions.choice_B: LayerNorm → Residual add → Self-attention → LayerNorm → Residual add → MLP
questions.choice_C: LayerNorm → Self-attention → Residual add → LayerNorm → MLP → Residual add
questions.choice_D: MLP → LayerNorm → Self-attention → Residual add → Residual add

questions.question: Why does the attention mechanism scale poorly to very long sequences in standard transformers?
questions.choice_A: Number of parameters grows quadratically with sequence length
questions.choice_B: The MLP layers become the computational bottleneck at long lengths
questions.choice_C: Positional encodings cannot represent positions beyond a fixed limit
questions.choice_D: Computational and memory cost of forming attention weights is $\mathcal{O}(n^2)$ in sequence length $n$

questions.question: In self-attention, what do the attention weights represent after applying softmax to the scaled dot products?
questions.choice_A: A probability distribution over keys/values indicating how much each token contributes to the query's representation
questions.choice_B: Normalized distances between tokens in embedding space
questions.choice_C: Fixed positional biases independent of content
questions.choice_D: Gradient magnitudes for backpropagation through time

questions.question: What is the role of cross-attention in encoder–decoder transformers (e.g., for machine translation)?
questions.choice_A: To enforce causal masking in the encoder
questions.choice_B: To allow the decoder to attend to encoder outputs when generating each target token
questions.choice_C: To tie parameters between encoder and decoder
questions.choice_D: To replace the decoder's MLP with a smaller module

questions.question: Why can decoder-only LLMs perform in-context learning from a prompt at inference time?
questions.choice_A: They fine-tune on the prompt before generating
questions.choice_B: They use bidirectional attention that reads future tokens
questions.choice_C: They are trained autoregressively to predict the next token given preceding context, so prompts condition the distribution over subsequent tokens
questions.choice_D: They dynamically change their parameters to store the prompt information

questions.question: In multi-head attention with model dimension $d_{model}$ and $h$ heads, how are projections typically structured for each head?
questions.choice_A: A shared projection for all heads with dimension $d_{model} \times d_{model}$
questions.choice_B: Separate $Q$ and a shared $K,V$ projection across all heads
questions.choice_C: One projection per token type to encourage sparsity
questions.choice_D: Each head uses its own $W_Q, W_K, W_V \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{model} \times d_k}$ where $d_k \approx d_{model}/h$, followed by a shared output projection $W_O$

questions.question: Which property of sinusoidal positional encodings is often cited as beneficial compared to learned absolute embeddings?
questions.choice_A: They enable the model to generalize to sequence lengths not seen during training due to their fixed functional form and relative shift properties
questions.choice_B: They reduce attention complexity from quadratic to linear
questions.choice_C: They eliminate the need for token embeddings
questions.choice_D: They guarantee perfect recovery of absolute positions from any subset of tokens

questions.question: What is a key benefit of residual connections in transformer blocks?
questions.choice_A: They force attention heads to be orthogonal
questions.choice_B: They improve gradient flow and allow deeper networks by providing short paths for signals
questions.choice_C: They decrease the number of parameters in the model
questions.choice_D: They remove the need for normalization layers

questions.question: Why is layer normalization generally preferred over batch normalization in transformer language models?
questions.choice_A: Batch normalization cannot be implemented on GPUs efficiently
questions.choice_B: Layer normalization requires no learned parameters
questions.choice_C: Layer normalization normalizes across features per token and is stable with variable-length sequences and small effective batch sizes common in sequence modeling
questions.choice_D: Batch normalization is incompatible with attention operations

questions.question: How does vocabulary size affect parameter counts in typical LLMs?
questions.choice_A: Only the attention layers scale with vocabulary size
questions.choice_B: Only the MLP layers scale with vocabulary size
questions.choice_C: Neither embeddings nor output layers depend on vocabulary size
questions.choice_D: Embedding and output (logit) projection matrices scale linearly with vocabulary size, contributing substantially to total parameters
